tests.what_was_measured: At recorded base, all five candidate regression cases failed; notably the GPU padding calculation returned 3 rather than the physical aligned extent 4.
At exact candidate 43c2db023064dfbfe823e0147be6b47d3fc06f2b, 14 focused tests passed on the prepared ROCm environment.

At the exact candidate, actual DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 planner behavior yielded four padded DSA rows but three expanded rows and no indexer/token-to-batch arrays; the candidate validator rejected this real planner-shaped state.

gpu_execution.evidence: Focused padding and independent planner-shape checks ran on AMD Instinct MI350X under ROCm 7.2.26015. This was metadata-level GPU execution, not an end-to-end DeepSeek model run.

remaining_counterexamples: For DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 planned at three real tokens and physically padded to four, the actual planner pads dsa_cache_seqlens_int32 but retains three-row dsa_seqlens_expanded and produces no indexer_k_start_end or token_to_batch_idx. The candidate validator rejects this state, so the eager speculative DSA path remains non-executable rather than validated end to end.
No evidence proves attention, indexer, DeepGEMM schedule metadata, top-k transforms, and KV writes all use a consistent declared physical or compact extent in a real speculative DSA execution.
remaining_limitations: No DeepSeek DSA weights or qualified end-to-end speculative DSA fixture were available. The tiny Llama fixture is architecturally inapplicable. CUDA-only and distributed paths were not exercised. No native source changed, so native rebuild was not applicable.
